name: Home Fitness Equipment
description: Size the market for connected home fitness equipment.
formula: SOM = Population x Penetration Rate x Purchase Frequency x Average Spend x Serviceable % x Obtainable Share %
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify addressable population = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply penetration rate = addressable_population x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate annual spend per user = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate TAM = penetrating_users x annual_spend_per_user
Step 5: Calculate SAM = TAM x serviceable_pct
Step 6: Calculate SOM = SAM x obtainable_share_pct
key_insight: Purchase frequency here is structurally low (about one unit per five years) because this is a durable good, not a consumable -- the market size lives or dies on penetration rate and price, not repeat frequency.
common_mistakes: Treating this like a subscription or consumable and inflating purchase frequency
Sizing off all households instead of the fitness-motivated addressable segment
Forgetting obtainable share -- connected fitness is a competitive category, not a blue ocean
framework_soundbite: A five-year replacement cycle means frequency isn't your lever -- penetration, price, and obtainable share are.
business_contexts: a connected fitness hardware startup evaluating market entry
a private equity firm sizing demand for home fitness equipment
question_patterns: A connected fitness hardware startup is deciding whether to enter the home equipment market and wants to size the annual revenue it could realistically capture against incumbents.

prompts.advanced: A private equity firm is evaluating a home fitness equipment brand whose growth thesis depends on post-pandemic demand persisting at levels the firm's consumer analysts are skeptical of. Build an independent serviceable-obtainable-market view before the bid deadline.
prompts.beginner: Estimate the serviceable obtainable market for connected home fitness equipment, accounting for realistic competitive capture.
prompts.intermediate: A connected fitness hardware startup is deciding whether to enter the home equipment market and wants to size the annual revenue it could realistically capture against incumbents.

approach_guidance.top_down_why: Start from households, narrow to the fitness-motivated segment, apply penetration and obtainable share, then multiply by price -- narrowing down from the national household count.
approach_guidance.bottom_up_why: Or start from one fitness-motivated household: their spend on a five-year replacement cycle, then scale up by how many households this brand can realistically win. Builds from the unit purchase instead of the population.
